subject.title: perf(logging): flush file transport asynchronously off the request path

question: Should OpenClaw accept bounded asynchronous file logging that can drop records during overload or after the graceful-shutdown timeout, and if so should its drain remain a core-only lifecycle capability rather than a plugin SDK API?
rationale: The performance benefit is plausible, but the acceptable durability tradeoff and the permanence of a plugin-visible shutdown control are operational product contracts rather than mechanical implementation details.

options.title: Approve a core-only transport
options.body: Move the drain behind a core lifecycle seam, retain the bounded transport, and document the approved overload and shutdown-loss behavior.

options.title: Preserve stronger durability
options.body: Redesign the transport and shutdown behavior so normal overload and graceful exit do not discard records before adopting it.

options.title: Defer the change
options.body: Pause the asynchronous transport until an owner defines the intended file-log durability contract.

recommendation.title: Approve a core-only transport
recommendation.body: Move the drain behind a core lifecycle seam, retain the bounded transport, and document the approved overload and shutdown-loss behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They have carried the current transport and follow-up test revisions and are the best available routing candidate from the supplied history.
